body.title: feat: add migration testing
body.body:
Follows the Frappe engineering handbook's migration testing guidance: build a site on an old version, seed it with realistic data, then walk it up one version at a time running bench migrate.

The ladder is anchored on LMS's own versions rather than the framework's, which is the handbook's FAQ case for apps that did not follow Frappe versioning. It starts from a site created on v2.0.0 (2024-07-10, the frappe v15 era) and climbs to the line the PR targets, moving frappe, payments and lms together at every hop. LMS declares required_apps = ["frappe/payments"], so payments cannot be dropped the way erpnext drops it before its ladder.

The seed exists because migrations over empty tables always succeed even when the change is invalid. It only touches doctypes and fields present at v2.0.0, and runs from outside the installed app so it can seed a site on much older code. Hop 1 replays all 94 patches in v2_0 against a populated database, which has not been done before.

Two departures from erpnext's patch.yml:

- Assertions, not just exit status. A patch that silently drops or orphans rows exits 0. Each hop compares row counts against what the seed recorded and re-resolves lesson -> chapter -> course and enrollment -> course. The v17 doctype deletions and medium -> delivery_mode rename are exactly the changes this is meant to catch.
- Redis service containers on bench's default ports instead of honcho, so no process has to be killed and restarted between hops.

Note that nothing under .github/ is linted by pre-commit here: the config's `exclude: 'node_modules|.git'` is unanchored, so `.git` matches `.github/` too. These files were checked with the pinned ruff directly.

body.title: fix(assignment): reset submission view when switching assignments
body.body:
edit: Partly fixes #2734

### Problem
On the learner assignment view, navigating from an assignment that **has** a submission to a **different** assignment shows the first assignment's submission (uploaded file / answer / comments) on the second — even though the second assignment has no submission of its own (its View Submissions list stays empty). It's display-only (no real submission is created), which is confusing for both learners and evaluators.

### Root cause
`pages/AssignmentSubmission.vue` renders `<Assignment>` **without a `:key`**, and `components/Assignment.vue` binds `assignment` / `submissionResource` to the initial props (no `watch` to refetch on prop change) and never resets `answer` / `attachment` / `comments`. So when the route params change, the component is reused and keeps the previously viewed assignment's state.

### Fix
Add a `:key` on `<Assignment>` (`assignmentID` + `submissionName`) so it remounts fresh whenever the assignment or submission changes — resetting all local state and refetching the correct submission. One line, no other behavior change.

### Testing
- Reproduced on a learner account (submitted assignment A, not B): opening A, then navigating to B, showed A's uploaded file on B. With the fix, B shows an empty "new" submission.
- The existing `assignmentStudentView` tests exercise the iframe-URL/Student-View path and are unaffected. Happy to add a component-remount regression test in whatever pattern you prefer.

cc @pateljannat

body.title: fix(profile): stop marking the profile image as mandatory
body.body: Follow-up to #2656: the Profile Image label still shows the required asterisk, even though a profile saves fine without an image. ### What happens 1. Open your profile and click **Edit Profile**. 2. Look at the **Profile Image** label. 3. **It's marked required**, but saving without an image works. ### Why #2656 removed `:required="true"` from the `` in `ProfileEditForm.vue` so that only First Name is required. But `Uploader.vue` sets `required: true` as a default in `withDefaults`. Leaving the prop off doesn't make it `false`; the default applies instead, so the asterisk stayed. Every other caller sets the prop explicitly (`BatchForm.vue` and `NewCourseForm.vue` pass `:required="false"`, `JobForm.vue` passes `:required="true"`). The profile form is the only one that relies on the default. ### Fix Pass `:required="false"` explicitly.

body.title: feat(frontend): adopt frappe-ui Password, Spinner, Alert, ErrorMessage and CodeEditor
body.body:
Part 2 of the `frappe-ui` adoption. Replaces the remaining hand-rolled components with library equivalents, fixes the evaluation calendar config, and addresses two existing payment gateway form bugs found while testing.

No breaking changes.

## What changed

### Password

Replaced plain `FormControl` usage with `Password` for secret fields.

Updated the relevant call sites across:

- `SettingsFields`
- `PaymentGatewayForm`
- `Services`

Also removed an unreachable schema branch relying on `secret: true`, since no schema in `src` uses it.

### Spinner

Replaced the last raw `animate-spin` usage in `ProctoringMonitor`.

### Alert

Replaced 5 hand-rolled notices across:

- `Assignment`
- `UpcomingEvaluations`
- `LiveClass`

One visible difference: `Alert` uses a neutral container background and themes the icon instead, so these notices no longer have amber, red, or blue backgrounds.

Existing translated copy is unchanged.

### ErrorMessage

Replaced 2 hand-rolled error blocks in:

- `RuleConditions`
- `Billing`

### CodeEditor

Replaced the custom Ace-based `Controls/CodeEditor.vue` with `frappe-ui`'s `CodeEditor`.

This removes:

- The custom Ace wrapper
- The `ace-builds` dependency
- The Ace bundle from the build

Editor height is now controlled using `--cm-max-height`.

This also fixes `settingsFieldsRequired.test.ts` hitting Vitest's default timeout while transforming Ace.

### Calendar

`ProfileEvaluationSchedule.vue` was already using `frappe-ui`'s `Calendar`, but its config contained invalid or ineffective options.

Removed:

- `redundantCellHeight`
- `disableModes`

Kept:

- `enableShortcuts: false`

`redundantCellHeight` is not a valid `CalendarConfig` key. The actual option is `hourHeight`, but switching to it would change the calendar's row height, so that is left out of this migration.

`disableModes` only affected the default header, which this page replaces.

Added tests that validate the config against the actual `CalendarConfig` keys.

Also added spacing below the **My availability** heading so the timezone text no longer runs into it.

### Payment gateway form

Two existing issues were found while testing this branch.

#### Secret fields rendered as plain text

Some provider doctypes define credentials as `Data` instead of `Password`, so they were rendered as plain inputs.

Secret fields are now detected by field name as well as fieldtype for names containing:

- `secret`
- `token`
- `password`
- `passphrase`
- `salt`

A bare `key` is intentionally not treated as secret because fields such as `publishable_key`, `api_key`, and `public_key` may be intended for browser use.

This only changes presentation. Fields defined as `Data` are still stored unencrypted by Frappe.

body.title: test: freeze nowdate() alongside getdate() in the evaluator schedule tests
body.body:
`get_schedule()` builds its date window using `nowdate()` and then iterates over it with `getdate()`.

The tests already froze `getdate()` and `nowtime()`, but `nowdate()` was still using the real clock. If a test crossed midnight between those calls, the schedule could start on a different day from the one used by the assertions.

This change adds an `EVALUATOR_NOWDATE` patch target and freezes `nowdate()` to the same date as `getdate()` in:

* `test_schedule_day_and_time`
* `test_schedule_dates`
* `TestTodaysSlots`

`TestTodaysSlots` had the same issue: its schedule window could start a day later than the date used by its assertions, causing all of today's slots to disappear.

As a regression check, moving the mocked `nowdate()` forward by one day causes `test_schedule_dates` and both `TestTodaysSlots` tests to fail.

`test_schedule_day_and_time` still passes with that shift, so freezing `nowdate()` there is defensive and keeps the mocked clocks consistent.

Test-only change. No runtime or UI changes.

body.title: feat(frontend): adopt frappe-ui components
body.body:
## Summary

This PR replaces several LMS-specific UI implementations with components that now exist in `frappe-ui`.

Overall, it removes more code than it adds: **45 files changed, +937 / -1153**.

This is part 1 of a larger migration. There are no breaking changes; everything removed here was internal to LMS and had no external callers.

## Changes

- **Command palette**
  Replaces the local command palette implementation with frappe-ui's `CommandPalette` components.

  LMS now only owns the parts specific to it: result/category sources and the Ctrl/Cmd+K trigger.

  `CommandPaletteGroup.vue` is removed.

- **Controls cleanup**
  Removes `Common/DateRange.vue`. An existing `getFormattedDateRange` helper already handled the formatting, while the component only added an icon and wrapper.

  Removes `Controls/MultiSelect.vue`, which had no imports.

  Also fixes a `ChildTable` bug: the component did not declare the `placeholder` prop passed by its caller. Because of this, the Programming Exercise form showed **"Add Row"** instead of **"Add Test Case"**.

- **First form migrated to FormLayout**
  Rebuilds `AnnouncementForm` using `FormLayout` from `@framework/ui`.

  This serves as the reference implementation for the remaining 11 forms, which will be migrated in follow-up PRs.

  Adds `components/FormLayout/RichTextEditorField.vue` so the LMS rich text editor can be used as a FormLayout field.

- **Remove Form labeling indirection**
  Deletes `components/Form/labeling.ts`, which only re-exported five names from `frappe-ui/experimental`.

  The ~20 files using it now import those APIs directly from the library.

- **Theme selection**
  Replaces the Light/Dark toggle in the sidebar user menu with a submenu containing:
  - Light
  - Dark
  - System

  The current option is marked with a tick.

  The code already supported the `system` preference, but there was previously no way to select it from the UI.

  The theme label is also now translatable instead of being hardcoded in English.

- **Tests**
  Adds:
  - `childTable.test.ts` for the add-button label fix
  - `userDropdownTheme.test.ts` for the theme menu

  The command palette test suites now share a common helper.

body.title: test: build server-test fixtures once per class and drop duplicate cases
body.body:
## Why

- The base test class did not roll back database changes after each test.
- Because of that, many test classes had to recreate and manually delete their own fixtures.
- This added repeated setup work and made tests more dependent on cleanup being correct.
- User creation and deletion is one of the more expensive parts of the suite, so repeating it across tests adds noticeable overhead.

## What changed

- Run every test inside a database savepoint and roll it back afterward.
- Build fixtures that can be shared once per test class instead of recreating them for every test.
- Remove tests that were already fully covered by another named test.
- Fix auth and progress tests so their assertions match what they claim to test.
- Replace repeated test cases with table-driven `subTest` cases where appropriate.
- Verify that violation-log severity is actually persisted to the database.
- Clear caches that are not reverted by a database rollback.
- Keep table-driven tests only where the cases genuinely share the same structure.

## How this was checked

- Ran the affected test suite after each change.
- Verified the rebuilt commits produce the same trees as the original commits.
- Confirmed `git diff backup HEAD` is empty.
- Confirmed the working tree is clean.

body.body:
Fills all 435 empty entries in lms/locale/ru.po. The file was 77% translated (1460 of 1895); it is now complete.

Product names are kept as-is (Zoom, Google Meet, Moodle, Canvas, Kajabi, Notion, Teachable, Thinkific, TalentLMS, Frappe Learning), as are literal field names in validation messages ("name must be a string" and friends), since those refer to API fields rather than UI labels.

Also fixes three entries flagged `python-format` that actually use brace format: `{0}% complete`, `You got {0}% correct answers...` and `You will have to get {0}% correct answers...`. In the msgid the `%` happens to be followed by `c`, which msgfmt accepts as the `%c` conversion specifier, so the mistake stays invisible in English. Any translation whose next word does not start with a valid specifier letter — every Cyrillic one, for instance — then fails `msgfmt --check`. Two of those three were already broken before this change: `msgfmt --check` did not pass on ru.po as it stood. It does now.

body.title: chore: upgrade frappe-ui to 1.0.0-beta.69
body.body:
## Summary

- Upgrades `frappe-ui` from `1.0.0-beta.29` to `1.0.0-beta.69` and moves the LMS frontend onto frappe-ui's v1 component API.
- Also bumps `lucide-static` from `1.17.0` to `^1.31.0`, which the new icon plugin needs.
- Fixes what the upgrade broke along the way: clipped tab icons, an overlapping Chapters header, a page-length dropdown with no options, and a lost table row height.
- Picks up the new espresso v2 colour palette: badges move from orange to amber, corner radii get numbered names.
- 218 files, 20 commits. 1694/1694 frontend tests pass, `yarn build` exits 0.

## Why

- We were 40 beta releases behind. frappe-ui v1 renamed props, slots and import paths across most of the component set, so the gap only gets more expensive to close.
- Staying behind also blocks the newer component families (charts, editor) that ship only in recent betas.

## Breaking changes

Anyone with custom frontend code or an in-flight frontend PR will hit these. What changed and what to do:

- **`frappe-ui/frappe` imports** — now come from `@framework/ui`.
- **Parked component families** — `Calendar`, the chart components, the `ListView` family and `TextEditor` now import from `frappe-ui/experimental` rather than the package root.
- **Popover-family slot API** — `toggle(flag)` is now `setOpen(value)`. Affects `Popover`, `Dropdown`, `DatePicker`, `Combobox`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `ContextMenu` and `HoverCard`.
- **`FileUploader`** — takes flat props instead of a nested `uploadArgs` object.
- **Tooltip and HoverCard delays are now milliseconds, not seconds.** This one is worth reading twice: `:hoverDelay="1.5"` still compiles, still runs, and now means 1.5 milliseconds instead of 1.5 seconds. Nothing warns you. Multiply every existing delay by 1000.
- **Design tokens** — removed radius aliases were renamed to numbered tokens, and the chromatic ink tokens shifted. Custom components using the old names will render with no radius rather than error.

## What's in it

- Dependency bump plus the build config it touches (vite, tailwind, `main.js`).
- `frappe-ui/frappe` imports moved to `@framework/ui`; parked families moved to `frappe-ui/experimental`.
- Overlays moved to the v1 API: Dialog, Tooltip, Popover, Dropdown, HoverCard, SettingsDialog.
- `FileUploader` on flat props, with an audit of every upload site to confirm each file still gets the public/private setting it had before.
- Token codemods: radius aliases renamed, ink tokens shifted, and the token parser taught to read OKLCH — it assumed hex, and the new palette ships OKLCH. Its alpha channel was also being computed gamma-encoded instead of linearly.
- Badges orange to amber, alerts stateless, tabs recomposed, shortcut combos on the v1 format.
- `debounce()` gained `.cancel()`, now used to drop the command palette's in-flight search when the query changes.
- Test mocks updated across 92 files; Playwright e2e selectors repaired.
- Tab strip fixes on course and batch detail pages (see below).
- Second bump, beta.65 to beta.69, with the `setOpen` rename and the delay unit conversion.

## Follow up
- More components are going to be ported from fui, this is simply basic migration of apis and colors

body.title: fix: preserve batch discussion hash in notifications
body.body: ## Description Fixes batch discussion notifications opening an invalid batch URL. When a user clicks a notification related to a batch discussion, the notification link contains a fragment such as: ```text /lms/batches/my-batch#discussions ``` However, `NotificationPanel.vue` currently passes the last part of the URL directly as the `batchName` route parameter: ```js router.push({ name: 'BatchDetail', params: { batchName: link.pop() }, }) ``` This causes Vue Router to treat: ```text my-batch#discussions ``` as the batch name itself and URL-encode the `#` character. The resulting URL becomes: ```text /lms/batches/my-batch%23discussions ``` instead of: ```text /lms/batches/my-batch#discussions ``` ## Result The invalid URL causes the Batch Detail page to load incorrectly. Observed symptoms include: - blank batch page - dashboard statistics showing zero - student details not opening correctly - subsequent tab navigation producing URLs such as: ```text /lms/batches/my-batch#discussions#dashboard ``` ## Fix Split the batch name and URL fragment before navigating and pass the fragment through Vue Router's `hash` property: ```js const batchTarget = link.pop() const [batchName, hashValue] = batchTarget.split('#') router.push({ name: 'BatchDetail', params: { batchName }, hash: hashValue ? `#${hashValue}` : '', }) ``` This preserves the intended URL: ```text /lms/batches/my-batch#discussions ``` ## Testing Tested with Frappe Learning 2.61.0. Verified the issue and fix using: - an instructor account - a student account - batch discussion notifications - navigation between Discussions and other Batch Detail tabs After the fix, clicking a discussion notification correctly opens the Discussions tab and subsequent tab navigation works normally. ## Screenshots 1. body.title: fix: translate the labels in the user menu
body.body:
## The problem

Seven entries in the user dropdown are plain strings rather than `__('...')`, so they stay English no matter how complete a translation is:

```js
label: 'My Profile',
label: 'Toggle Theme',
label: 'Settings',
label: 'Clear Demo Data',
label: 'Login to Frappe Cloud',
label: 'Log out',
label: 'Log in',
```

"Toggle Theme" sitting in English next to a fully translated sidebar is the most visible case — the menu is the first thing a user opens.

## Why wrapping is safe here

`userDropdownOptions` is a `computed`, evaluated at render time, when `translationPlugin` has already installed `window.__`. The identical change inside a top-level constant would throw `__ is not a function` at module load — worth keeping in mind for the nav link constants elsewhere, which is why this PR does not touch them.

## Translations

Four labels resolve from frappe's own dictionary once wrapped. The other four had nowhere to resolve from: without `__()` the extractor never saw them, so no PO entries existed at all. Added, with Russian translations.

`msgfmt --check` passes.

body.title: feat: show which topic a question came from
body.body:
## Why

A quiz that draws from a large bank mixes questions from every module, and the question header gives no hint which one is being asked about. The learner only finds out where they are weak from the final summary — too late to slow down on the topic they are shaky in.

This is most noticeable with `shuffle_questions` + `limit_questions_to`, where each attempt is a fresh sample across the whole bank.

## What

- an optional `topic` field on **LMS Question**
- rendered in the question header, opposite the marks

Empty by default, so existing quizzes look exactly as they do today.

The value goes through `__()`: a bank filled in by a course author is likely to carry topic names worth translating.

## Note

I am using this downstream through a Custom Field plus a small frontend patch, which works but means every author who wants it has to rediscover it. Upstreaming the field seemed more useful than keeping the workaround. Happy to adjust the placement or the label if you would rather have it elsewhere — for instance as a Link to a proper Topic doctype, if that fits your plans better than free text.

Fixes #635

## Why

A lesson is only reachable through its chapter, but the lesson form never showed which chapter it belonged to. With similar lesson names across chapters there was no way to tell which chapter's lesson was open — the outline sidebar has the answer, the editor itself does not.

## What

Show the chapter title above the lesson title.

No API change needed. `lms.lms.utils.get_lesson_creation_details` already returns `chapter.title`; the form was simply not reading it.

```js
const chapterTitle = computed(() => lessonDetails.data?.chapter?.title)
```

It renders only when a title is present, so the layout is unchanged if the chapter has no title.

`frontend/src/tests/lessonChapterTitle.test.ts`, using the existing `lessonFormTeardown.test.ts` harness:

- shows the chapter the lesson belongs to
- shows it above the lesson title, not in place of it
- renders nothing when the chapter has no title

All three fail without the change.

Full suite run before and after — identical apart from the new tests. The 35 pre-existing file failures on `develop` (settings, profile, raven, multiLink) are unrelated and reproduce on a clean checkout.

|---|---|---|
| `develop` | 35 failed / 114 passed | 12 failed / 1199 passed |
| this branch | 35 failed / 115 passed | 12 failed / 1202 passed |

`LessonForm.vue` is not Prettier-clean on `develop`, so I did not run Prettier over the whole file — it would bury this change in unrelated reformatting. The added lines match Prettier's output, and the new test file is Prettier-clean.

A lesson is only reachable through its chapter, but the lesson form never showed which chapter it belonged to. const chapterTitle = computed(() => lessonDetails.data?.chapter?.title)

body.title: fix: let a student reach the evaluation scheduler on a course
body.body:
The certification page read the course title and evaluator with
frappe.client.get_value on LMS Course, which LMS Student has no read
permission for. 

The call failed, `courses` never populated, and
UpcomingEvaluations never rendered, so a learner who had bought a
certificate had no way to book an evaluation and saw a page with no title.
get_certification_details now returns the title and the evaluator, and the
page takes the enrollment and the certificate from that same call.

The evaluator is a staff email address, so it is only returned once the
certificate has been paid for. The title is not gated: any signed-in user
could already read it through this endpoint's sibling fields.

The page is now TypeScript and shares CertificationInfo with
CertificationLinks rather than describing the response twice. It reports a
failed load instead of rendering an empty page, and skips the request for a
guest, who this route admits and the endpoint rejects.

Regression tests in test_certification_api.py and courseCertification.test.ts.

body.title: fix: carry contact-us images inside the email instead of linking them
body.body:
## Summary

- Paste an image into the Contact Us form and the recipient saw a broken image.
- The editor uploads pasted images as private files, and the email carried only a link to one. A private file link needs a logged-in account with permission to open it, which a recipient's mail app does not have.
- Images now travel inside the email as proper inline attachments, the way Gmail does it. The file stays private and nothing is made publicly readable.
- Frappe already supports this: an image marked with `embed` instead of `src` becomes a real inline attachment. The pattern is copied from Helpdesk's `HDTicket.parse_content`.

## Security

- Only files the sender is actually allowed to read are attached. This matters because the framework function that reads the file off disk performs no permission check of its own.
- The bytes come from the file record the sender has permission on, and that same record supplies the address written into the email. Nothing the browser sends is used to look up a file on disk.
- **This was caught in review of an earlier revision of this PR — it is not a flaw in `develop`.** That revision matched the browser's text against the database and then let the framework re-open the same text as a path. The two do not agree: the database column ignores letter case, the filesystem does not. So a user could upload their own `Offer-Letter.pdf`, reference someone else's `offer-letter.pdf`, pass the check against their own file, and have the other person's file read and emailed. Closed.
- The number of embedded images and their total size are now capped, because the email is assembled while the user's request is still waiting.

## Other fixes included

- A message that is only a pasted image, with no text, used to be rejected as empty. That is the commonest way people use this form, and it now works.
- The email carries the cleaned-up version of the message that gets saved, rather than the raw text from the browser, so scripts and dangerous links cannot reach the recipient's inbox.
- Replies can be matched back to the saved record — a message id was missing.
- Embedded images are linked to the saved record, so staff viewing the message later see it correctly.
- Sending goes through a new server endpoint that takes the recipient address from LMS Settings, instead of the browser telling the server who to email.

body.title: fix: stop offering evaluation slots that have already started today
body.body:
- **The problem**: Students book certificate evaluations by picking a time slot. The picker showed today's slots that had already gone past — at 14:47 it offered today's 09:30, 12:00 and 14:00 — and submitting one failed with "You cannot schedule evaluations for past slots." Slots on future days worked fine, so the error hit the slots shown first.

- **Root cause**: The slot list was built from today's date without ever comparing slot times against the clock. The validation that runs on submit does compare them. The two disagreed on what was bookable.

- **The fix**: A new `slot_has_started` helper drops today's lapsed slots before the list is built, using the same strict "earlier than now" comparison as the validation. A slot starting exactly now is still bookable, and the list now matches what a booking will accept.

- **Testing**: 4 new tests in `test_course_evaluator.py::TestTodaysSlots`. Three fail on the parent commit; the fourth is a deliberate control that passes either way, so a fix that broke the boundary would show up. One of the tests books every slot the picker offers with the clock pinned in both modules, checking the list and the validation against each other rather than separately.

- **Also included**: the shared test helper `_create_evaluator` reused an existing record without refreshing its "unavailable from/to" dates. Those are written relative to the day the record was created, so on a long-lived test site they went stale and swallowed dates other tests compute from today. This was already making an unrelated test fail in a way that looked like a date bug. Fixed, which takes that suite from 24/25 to 25/25.

- **Known limits**:
  - The picker and the validation each read the clock at their own moment, so a slot can still lapse in the seconds between the page rendering and the student submitting.
  - The validation has another rule the picker still does not mirror: a student who already has an upcoming evaluation for that course sees a full slot list and is rejected on submit. Same kind of problem, different rule, not fixed here.

body.title: feat(raven)!: sync channel membership from LMS rules (backport #2706)
body.body:
## What this adds

Settings > Raven, where a moderator maps LMS to Raven workspaces and channels and
says who belongs in each one. Membership follows the rules: when a student
enrols or an instructor is tagged on a course, the sync adds them to the channel
on the next pass, and removes them when they stop matching.

A rule reads as a cascade. The first choice names who, and every answer narrows
what the next one offers, so no control on screen is one the current answer has
made meaningless.

```
Student  →  All                                          (holds the LMS Student role)
         →  Enrolled  →  payment  →  Any | Batches | Courses | Both  →  pick records

Staff    →  All                                          (the three platform roles)
         →  Platform role  →  Course Creator | Evaluator | Moderator
         →  Assigned on    →  Instructor | Evaluator  →  scope  →  pick records
```

Conditions combine with and/or and nest one level, on the framework's own
ConditionBuilder.

## Needs frappe/raven_integration first

The LMS provider declares `depends_on: {value_in: [...]}`, a set form this branch
adds to the registry. An older registry rejects it at load with "declares
depends_on with no value", which takes out every Raven rule on the site. Merge
the raven_integration branch first, or together with this one.

## Breaking: the rule vocabulary changed

Four flat rule types became two cascading ones. A rule stored against the old
vocabulary is detected on load, blocked from saving, and skipped rather than
evaluated, with a message saying it was written for an older version and has to
be replaced.

That detection is a positive schema match, not a list of known-bad values,
because of one case that does not fail on its own terms. The old `Evaluator`
meant every `Course Evaluator` record; it would now mean holders of the
`Batch Evaluator` role. On the bench I measured those at 23 and 15 people,
overlapping by 10. Left to resolve, that rule would have moved 18 people in and
out of a channel with no error anywhere.

## UI

body.title: feat: allow chart colors to be themed via CSS custom properties (--chart-1..--chart-5)
body.body:
### Problem

The frontend can be restyled almost entirely through CSS custom properties, but chart series colors can't:

- `AxisChart`/`DonutChart` call sites that pass no `colors` (Statistics page, admin batch dashboard) fall back to ECharts' built-in palette, which no CSS can reach.
- Pages that do pass colors hardcode a per-page list (course dashboard pie, program progress summary donut).

So a theme with no blue in it still gets blue charts.

### Solution

Opt-in theme tokens, with the current behavior kept intact as fallback:

- New util `frontend/src/utils/chartColors.ts`: `getChartColors(count)` reads `--chart-1` .. `--chart-5` from the root element's computed style and returns the defined values in order — or `undefined` when none are defined.
- Call sites only pass `colors` when tokens exist:
  - `Statistics.vue` — 3× AxisChart + 1× DonutChart get `colors` via conditional spread.
  - `AdminBatchDashboard.vue` — AxisChart, same conditional spread.
  - `ProgramProgressSummary.vue` — DonutChart prefers tokens; the existing `var(--red-400)`/`--amber-400`/`--pink-400`/`--blue-400`/`--green-400` list stays as the fallback.
  - `CourseDashboard.vue` — `progressColors` prefers tokens with the existing red/amber/blue/green list as fallback. The legend dots next to the pie now read from the same `progressColors` by index, so legend and pie stay in sync when a theme overrides the tokens (identical output by default: the backend returns the distribution in a fixed order that matches the previous name-based mapping in `get_progress_distribution`).

When no `--chart-N` token is defined, nothing changes — the spread contributes nothing and the fallback lists are the ones already in the code.

Notes:
- Values are resolved through `getComputedStyle`, so any valid CSS color works, and ECharts receives concrete colors (it can derive emphasis/dimmed variants from them).
- Tokens are read once at component setup.

Context: we (LetItGrowth) run the LMS in production re-themed entirely via CSS custom properties; the charts are currently the only surface that theming approach cannot recolor, which is what motivated this change.

`yarn build` passes; touched files verified against Prettier (no formatting drift on the changed lines).

body.body:
When opening the Batches page, the footer was supposed to show 
how many batches match the current filters (like "8 of 24"). 
Instead it was throwing an error and nothing would load.

The issue was in how we were counting the batches behind the 
scenes. We were using an older way of doing it that no longer 
works with the current version of Frappe. 

Updated the count_matching function in utils.py to use a 
different approach that works correctly,  it now builds the 
filtered query first and runs a count on top of it, so the 
footer shows the right number every time without crashing.

body.title: fix: reveal the signup result banners on released frappe
body.body: ### Problem #2691 inlined the `alert_banner` macro so `/login` stops returning a 500 on a released frappe. That part works — but the banners it renders never become visible. Sign-up succeeds or fails and the user sees nothing: the message lands in the DOM, correctly, and stays invisible. Two independent causes: **1. Released frappe hides them by default.** `login.bundle.scss` styles `.login-error-banner` / `.login-success-banner` completely — padding, gap, background, radius, colour, svg fill — but sets `display: none`, expecting its own JS to flip it. LMS only removed the `hidden` class, which does not touch `display`. **2. frappe's own JS re-hides them.** `login.js` binds a page-wide handler: ```js $(".page-card-body input").on("input", function () { $(this).closest(".page-card-body").removeClass("invalid").find(".login-error-banner").hide(); }); ``` The LMS form has its own `.page-card-body`, so it is caught by that selector. jQuery's `.hide()` writes an **inline** `display: none`, which outranks any stylesheet rule — so once the user has typed their email, no class toggle can reopen the banner. ### Fix Reveal with `.css("display", "flex")` rather than a class toggle. This is what frappe's own `login.show_error_banner` does, and being inline it clears the stamped `display: none` and outranks the stylesheet in a single step — no specificity war, and no assumption about which frappe version is running. The icon needed two smaller corrections: - **`width="16" height="16"` attributes** — neither frappe version sizes the banner svg in CSS; released frappe's own login markup carries these same attributes. - **`fill` moved from an attribute to an inline style** — frappe's `.login-*-banner svg { fill: var(--ink-red-4) }` overrides a presentation attribute, which fills in the stroked lucide glyph and renders the icon as a solid dot. No CSS is added. Both frappe versions already style these banners (released via `login.bundle.scss`, develop via `es-alert`); the only thing neither supplies is `display`. ### Screenshots **Error path — existing email** **Success path — new email** ### Tests Two regression tests added to `lms/tests/test_signup_form.py`, pinning the two decisions a future cleanup would most plausibly undo — the explicit `display`, and the inline `fill` / sized icon. Note that true visibility can only be asserted in a browser, and this repo has no guest-flow e2e harness (the cypress specs all assume a logged-in author). These tests guard the source-level decisions; the rendering itself was verified manually against a released frappe. ### Verification Checked end to end against frappe v16 on a live site, driving the real form: both banners report `display: flex`, `isVisible: true`, correct text, and correctly rendered outline icons.

body.title: feat(quiz): add availability scheduling for quizzes and assignments
body.body: ## Summary - Add opt-in **Enable Scheduling** on **LMS Quiz** and **LMS Assignment** - When enabled, **Schedule Start** is required and **Schedule End** is optional - Learners cannot start/submit before start; if end is set, they cannot start/submit after end - Enforced in the UI and on the server (`submit_quiz` / assignment submission validate) - Shared helpers in `lms/lms/schedule_utils.py` (+ tests) ## Motivation Instructors need a simple availability window so quizzes and assignments are only attemptable during a defined period, without relying on manual open/close. ## Screenshots ### Author — Quiz settings ### Author — Assignment form ### Learner — Quiz before start ### Learner — Quiz after end (optional end set) ### Learner — Assignment outside window ## Test plan - [ ] Scheduling off → quiz/assignment behave as before - [ ] Scheduling on, missing start → save rejected - [ ] End ≤ start → save rejected - [ ] Before start → learner cannot start quiz / submit assignment - [ ] After end → learner cannot start quiz / submit assignment - [ ] No end date → remains open after start - [ ] Student submit API blocked outside window; privileged grading still works
